mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% month-over-month, sustained for two months, signals supply-side stress that raises input costs and reduces output, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >1% MoM for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns remain positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their previous monthly maxima signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both set new monthly highs
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such dual-shock months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month coincident with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which precedes a negative S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days as profit margins are squeezed.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such overheating episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment and consumer confidence, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such housing-softening episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand components of GDP, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such dual-demand-contraction months.
